body: T20 - HINT SYSTEM ADHD CRITIQUE. Current system: 3 layers. Layer 1 HINT (text clue). Layer 2 SHOW ANSWER. Layer 3 SOLUTION STEPS. Layer 2 is hidden until Layer 1 clicked. Layer 3 hidden until Layer 2 clicked. CRITIQUE: The 3-layer progressive reveal is good for reducing hint dependency. But current implementation has one ADHD problem: the HINT button is always visible but the hint content is hidden. This means Kai sees a button with no visual state change after clicking - the hint text appears below but the button still says HINT. He may click it 3 times thinking it did not work. IMPROVEMENT SPEC: After clicking HINT, change button text to CLOSE HINT and add .active class with different background color. This gives immediate state feedback. Kai knows his click registered. Button text: HINT (default) -> CLOSE HINT (expanded). Color: ghost button (default) -> ghost button with rgba(255,255,255,0.1) background (expanded). This is the smallest change that closes the feedback gap. One CTA at a time rule: when HINT is expanded, SHOW ANSWER button should be visible (already is). When SOLUTION STEPS is expanded, both prior layers should show collapsed state. Currently they stay expanded. Add collapse-on-lower-layer to reduce visual clutter. EFFORT ESTIMATE: 3 small CSS additions + 2 JS state changes. Low risk.
